transcript.text: The missing number is 4 because you multiply both the top and bottom numbers of two-thirds by two to get the equivalent fraction with a denominator of six.
The answer is 4/6 because you multiply the top and bottom by 2 since the denominator doubled from 3 to 6. Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?
The answer is 6/9, which simplifies to 2/3, because when the denominators are the same, you just add the top numbers together.
Wait, why do we leave the bottom number alone? I still don't get why you only add the top numbers.

We leave the bottom number alone because the denominator just tells you the size of the equal pieces the whole is divided into, so adding fractions with the same bottom number just counts how many of those equal-sized pieces you have.
